basis: Static campaign topology review following the treasure/Rift-Crossed changes assessed in 0.202.0.json. New tiers start with five nodes instead of two or three, later floors range from one to five instead of two to four, with a meeting point every sixth floor and a five-way split afterward (or the final two Shrines when next). Shared vertical presentation does not change fight rules. More visible routes can improve reward targeting; mandatory meeting points reduce avoidance and can force an unfavourable encounter. Per-tier Elite and merchant placement caps, rewards, encounter scaling, floor counts, and one-stop-per-floor path length remain unchanged, but the new seeded graph changes placement and acquisition opportunities. Existing saved maps retain topology. All thirty Ascendancies and ten class starts retain previous unrated/unmeasured combat labels. Tier I-III access, IV-X developing setups, XI-XVI recovery and XVII-XX survival need real route-choice evidence. Opening, extended and beyond-ten-turn strength are not newly measured in either mode. No simulations or human matches were run. Mixed companion-HP/healing, Exposed/multi-hit and Consume/draw builds gain route options but face the same forced meeting points; no synergy or grade improvement is guaranteed.
